method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5) 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism' (18 March 2019). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © Medical Journal of Australia / AMPCo (free to read; the MJA copyright policy forbids reproduction without written consent) (read at https://www.mja.com.au/journal/copyright (the article page links 'Copyright and linking policy'; free-to-read full text retrieved 2026-09-23)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **VTE symptoms are non-specific: only about 20% of suspected cases are confirmed,** so actively seek the diagnosis and confirm it with imaging; misdiagnosis in either direction does harm.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wells or Geneva scores must be paired with D-dimer; neither alone can safely rule out VTE.** These rules are for outpatients and emergency departments, not inpatients. (GRADE strong, high)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PERC can rule out PE without more tests in patients under 50 when the expected PE rate is below 15%,** which applies in most Australian and New Zealand EDs; a positive PERC needs further work-up.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A negative D-dimer with a non-high clinical probability avoids imaging; a positive D-dimer alone proves nothing,** since it rises with cancer, inflammation, infection, trauma and pregnancy.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **DVT: a single negative ankle-to-groin duplex ultrasound generally excludes DVT.** A single repeat scan 3–6 months later, before stopping anticoagulation, gives a baseline for future symptoms; repeated scans without symptoms do not help.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PE: CTPA is the preferred test** (GRADE strong, high); VQ scanning suits renal impairment and is preferred in pregnancy. A normal VQ excludes PE, but 27–55% of scans are non-diagnostic and need leg ultrasound or CTPA.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Think of hidden cancer after an unprovoked VTE:** up to 10% are diagnosed with cancer within a year. Examine carefully and do age-appropriate screening; abdominopelvic CT adds nothing.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classify the event as provoked (surgical or non-surgical; transient or persistent) or unprovoked:** this sets recurrence risk and treatment length.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anticoagulate most VTE:** it cuts extension or recurrence by at least 80%. DOACs and warfarin work equally well (GRADE strong, high); DOACs are usually favoured as they need no routine monitoring.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For proximal DVT and PE, choose an oral factor Xa inhibitor (apixaban or rivaroxaban) over dabigatran or warfarin,** because no injectable lead-in is needed. (GRADE strong, high)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No DOACs in pregnancy or breastfeeding: use low molecular weight heparin.** In cancer-associated VTE, edoxaban or rivaroxaban match dalteparin for efficacy but bleed more, so they can be considered case by case.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Proximal DVT or PE: at least 3 months for everyone.** If the cause was major surgery or trauma that has resolved, stop at 3 months. (GRADE strong)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unprovoked, or provoked by a transient non-surgical factor: treat 3–6 months, then decide whether to extend.** Recurrent events (two or more), active cancer or antiphospholipid syndrome warrant extended anticoagulation.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Distal DVT:** anticoagulation benefit is uncertain; two duplex scans over 2 weeks is a reasonable alternative, especially with high bleeding risk. Most distal DVT is treated for 6–12 weeks, and 6 weeks if a major provoking factor has resolved.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extending beyond 3 months** lowers recurrence by at least 80% during treatment, for a major bleeding risk under 1% a year; the benefit ends when treatment stops. Weigh bleeding against recurrence, with the patient's preference.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For extended therapy, consider a lower DOAC dose:** apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily works as well as 5.0 mg twice daily beyond 6 months, and rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily as well as 20 mg once daily. Either DOAC dose is preferred over warfarin. Avoid aspirin (100 mg daily) unless anticoagulation is impossible: it prevents far less recurrence yet bleeds like rivaroxaban 10 mg. (GRADE strong, high)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrence predictors that drive most decisions:** unprovoked or persistent-factor events (vs surgical), PE or proximal DVT (vs distal), prior VTE, and male sex.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bleeding risk:** active or recent (under 30 days) bleeding usually rules out anticoagulation. Other predictors: prior bleeding (especially on anticoagulants), a bleeding lesion such as peptic ulcer, surgery in the last 14 days, active cancer and severe kidney disease.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not test routinely for inherited thrombophilia:** factor V Leiden and prothrombin gene heterozygosity change neither duration nor family advice. Testing for antiphospholipid syndrome after unprovoked VTE is reasonable. (GRADE strong, moderate)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspect CTEPH if breathlessness persists over the 2 years after PE** (incidence 3.4%): arrange a VQ scan and echocardiogram. Untreated, 5-year survival is 30%.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Post-thrombotic syndrome affects one in three after DVT;** anticoagulation does not prevent it, and compression stockings are for symptom relief of swelling and pain only.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Thrombolysis (or an alternative) is for massive, haemodynamically unstable PE;** invasive clot removal otherwise has a limited role. An IVC filter is only for acute VTE with an absolute contraindication to anticoagulation, not for anticoagulated patients. (GRADE strong)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23
